description: Canonical Galaxy device troubleshooting knowledge base. Each record in 'troubleshooting_records' is one atomic, screen-level remediation action for a canonical issue, grounded in a specific cited source (see sources.json). Records marked source_type 'competition_spec' or 'provided_dataset' originate from materials supplied with this task. 'synthetic_query_variations' contains generated colloquial paraphrases used only to map informal user language to a canonical_issue -- these are NOT factual troubleshooting knowledge and carry no steps of their own; they are kept in a separate array from 'troubleshooting_records' per the task's zero-fabrication and separation requirements.

merged_variants: phone barely lasts half a day

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for Software and App Updates
troubleshooting_records.description: It will patch known battery-drain bugs
steps: Open Settings and tap Software update or System updates.
Tap Download and install (or Check for system updates).
Separately, open Galaxy Store or Play Store and update all apps.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Turn On Power Saving Mode
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reduce performance to save power
steps: Open Settings and tap Battery.
Tap Power saving.
Turn on the switch and select additional restrictions as needed.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Configure Background Usage Limits
troubleshooting_records.description: It will put unused apps to sleep automatically
steps: Open Settings, tap Battery, then Background usage limits.
Turn on Put unused apps to sleep.
Optionally choose Sleeping apps or Deep sleeping apps for specific apps.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Switch to Light Performance Profile
troubleshooting_records.description: It will prioritize battery life over speed
steps: Open Settings and tap Device care.
Tap Performance profile.
Select Light.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Optimize the Display for Power Saving
troubleshooting_records.description: It will lower screen-related power consumption
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Turn on Dark mode to reduce power use from a darker color scheme.
Lower the Brightness slider or turn off Adaptive brightness.
Tap Motion smoothness and select Standard to reduce refresh rate to 60Hz.
Tap Screen timeout and pick a shorter duration.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Disable or Schedule Always On Display
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop the screen waking unnecessarily
steps: Open Settings and tap Lock screen and AOD.
Turn off the switch at the top to disable Always On Display entirely, or
Tap When to show and choose Tap to show, As scheduled, or For new notifications.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Identify and Uninstall Battery-Draining Apps
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove apps consuming excess battery
steps: Open Settings and tap Battery.
Tap the battery usage graph to see per-app consumption.
Select the high-usage app and tap Uninstall, then confirm.

troubleshooting_records.description: It will check the physical battery condition
steps: Install the Samsung Members app if not already installed.
Open the Support tab and select Phone diagnostics.
Run the battery test and review results.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Samsung Members Phone diagnostics is referenced across multiple official Samsung pages; exact menu wording may vary by region and app version.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Force Restart the Device
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear temporary software glitches
steps: On devices with a Power button: hold Volume down and Power for ~10 seconds.
On devices with a Side button: hold Volume down and Side button for ~10 seconds.
When the Power menu or Samsung logo appears, continue holding until it reboots.
If Maintenance mode appears, use Volume buttons to select Normal Boot.

loses charge even when not in use
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Boot Into Safe Mode to Isolate a Rogue App
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reveal whether a downloaded app is draining battery
steps: Press and hold the Power button (or open Quick settings and tap the Power icon).
Touch and hold Power off until the Safe mode icon appears; tap Safe mode.
Use the device normally; if drain stops, a recently installed app is the likely cause.
Uninstall suspect apps one by one, then exit Safe mode by restarting normally.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Perform a Factory Data Reset (Last Resort)
troubleshooting_records.description: It will restore the device to original battery behavior
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Factory data reset
steps: Back up all data using Smart Switch or a cloud account.
Open Settings, search for and select Factory data reset.
Tap Factory data reset again, then Reset, and follow the prompts.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Erases all data; Samsung notes this is not a permanent fix if the root cause is an app awaiting a future update.

merged_variants: new phone battery drains fast in first days
new phone battery is bad during setup
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Understand Temporary Drain During Initial Setup
troubleshooting_records.description: It will explain expected first-days battery drop
steps: No user action required for a few days: initial setup, account sync, and restoring backups temporarily increase battery use.
If elevated drain continues beyond the first few days, follow the standard battery optimization steps.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Understand and Mitigate 5G-Related Battery Use
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reduce power used maintaining dual network links
steps: Note: 5G phones maintain a concurrent 3G/LTE link for call and message continuity, which increases drain.
Open Settings, then Connections, then Mobile networks to review network mode options if you want to limit 5G use.
Apply the standard battery optimization steps (Power saving, Background usage limits, display settings) alongside this.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Samsung's own text says Galaxy phones use AI-based software to help manage 5G power draw; no specific toggle to fully disable the dual-link behavior was documented in the source.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Inspect Charger, Cable, and Port for Damage or Debris
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out a physical connection fault
steps: Verify the phone, charger, and USB cable show no physical or liquid damage.
Check the USB connections for corrosion or bent pins.
Inspect the charging port for dust, lint, or debris that could block contact.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for Moisture in the Charging Port
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear moisture that blocks charging
steps: Check for a moisture-detected notification.
Gently shake the device to remove moisture from the port.
Wipe with a soft, clean cloth and air-dry in a well-ventilated area before retrying.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Applies to water-resistant Galaxy devices; the charging port must be fully dry even on water-resistant models.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Use a Genuine, Compatible Samsung Charger
troubleshooting_records.description: It will avoid slow charging from mismatched hardware
steps: Confirm the charger and cable are genuine Samsung accessories rated for your device.
For fast charging, ensure the charger supports Adaptive Fast Charging or the appropriate wattage.
Avoid third-party or damaged cables, which may cause unstable or slow charging.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Avoid Heavy Use While Charging
troubleshooting_records.description: It will prevent temperature-related charging slowdowns
steps: Close high-performance apps such as games, video streaming, or heavy browsing while charging.
Let the device charge at room temperature; avoid direct sun or very cold environments.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Soft-Reboot the Device
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear temporary software charging faults
steps: Press and hold the Power and Volume down keys together until the device restarts.
Reconnect the original charger once the device has restarted and check charging status.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Run Samsung Members Charging Diagnostics
troubleshooting_records.description: It will test cable, wireless, and battery status
steps: Open the Samsung Members app and tap Support.
Tap Get started to run Phone diagnostics.
Tap Battery status, Cable charging, or Wireless charging, then review the results.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Availability requires the Samsung Members app to be installed; feature set may vary by region.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Charge From a Wall Outlet for at Least an Hour
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out an extension cord or weak source
steps: Plug the charging cable directly into a wall outlet, not an extension cord or power strip.
Charge for at least 1 hour using the charger that came with the device.
Allow up to 10 minutes for the charging indicator to appear if the battery was fully drained.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Force-Start the Device After Deep Discharge
troubleshooting_records.description: It will attempt startup after a long-drained battery
steps: Disconnect the device from the charger.
Press and hold the Power button for 15-20 seconds to attempt a start.
If it turns on, reconnect the original charger and let it charge fully.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Escalate to Samsung Service if Charging Still Fails
troubleshooting_records.description: It will get a hardware inspection for persistent failure
steps: After completing software and cable checks, if the device still will not charge,
visit a Samsung walk-in service center, or
schedule a repair service online.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Use a High-Speed Charger for DeX Mode
troubleshooting_records.description: It will meet the power requirement DeX needs
steps: Confirm the charger outputs more than 9V/1.67A; DeX accessories require a high-speed charger.
Do not use battery packs, which are not compatible with DeX.
If DeX still won't launch, exit Maximum power saving mode first.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy devices with Samsung DeX support

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Inspect the Screen for Physical Damage
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out cracked-glass flicker causes
steps: Check the screen for cracks or shattered glass.
If damage is found, visit a Samsung walk-in service center or schedule a repair.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Disable Adaptive Brightness
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop brightness auto-adjustment from flickering
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Turn off the switch next to Adaptive brightness.
If flickering occurs at low brightness, manually raise the brightness slider.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Change the Motion Smoothness (Refresh Rate) Setting
troubleshooting_records.description: It will test if a high refresh rate causes flicker
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Tap Motion smoothness.
Select Standard (60Hz) instead of Adaptive/High to see if flickering stops.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Sourced from a Samsung Community moderator-style walkthrough plus general Samsung display-setting patterns; treat exact menu labels as approximate across One UI versions.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Boot Into Safe Mode to Rule Out a Third-Party App
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reveal whether an app is causing the flicker
steps: Hold the Power button until the power-off menu appears.
Touch and hold Power off until Safe mode appears, then tap it.
Use the device normally; if flickering stops, uninstall the most recently installed app first, repeating as needed.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for Software Updates
troubleshooting_records.description: It will apply display-bug fixes from Samsung
steps: Open Settings, tap Software update.
Tap Download and install to get the latest available update.

merged_variants: black bar moves across camera preview
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Understand Camera-Preview Flicker From Artificial Lighting
troubleshooting_records.description: It will explain flicker caused by LED/fluorescent lights
steps: Recognize that fluorescent or LED lighting can flicker faster than the eye perceives, which the camera shutter can pick up as banding.
Add more light to the scene to reduce the effect.
If flicker persists outside the Camera app too, treat it as a general display issue instead.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Reset an Individual App Showing Flicker
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear a corrupted app's display state
steps: Open Settings, tap Apps.
Select the app where flickering occurs.
Tap Reset (or Storage > Clear cache) for that app.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Apply the Galaxy S26/S26+ Specific Flicker Guidance
troubleshooting_records.description: It will address a model-specific flicker condition
steps: This applies specifically to the Galaxy S26 or S26+ under certain conditions such as playing HD video, using Google Photos, or editing QHD+ photos on the S26+.
Check for software updates first, as Samsung ships model-specific fixes through updates.
Follow the same update, app-update, and reboot sequence used for general software issues.
troubleshooting_records.notes: This is a model-specific official Samsung troubleshooting guide; do not apply this record's device scope claim to other models.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Escalate to Service if Flicker Persists in Safe Mode
troubleshooting_records.description: It will get hardware evaluated when software isn't the cause
steps: If flickering continues even in Safe Mode after all software steps, treat it as a likely hardware issue.
Contact the nearest Samsung Support Center to book an inspection or repair.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for Liquid Damage and Clean the Screen
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out surface or moisture causes of blur
steps: Check the device for signs of liquid exposure.
Clean the screen with a soft, dry, microfiber cloth to remove smudges or residue.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Source S046 was only referenced as a related-article link and was not independently fetched in full; treat step detail as indicative, not verified verbatim.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Adjust the Screen Resolution Setting
troubleshooting_records.description: It will raise or correct the rendered resolution
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Tap Screen resolution.
Select a higher resolution option (e.g., FHD+ or WQHD+ if supported) and apply.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Step content inferred from general Samsung display-settings conventions since the underlying article (S046) was not fully fetched; requires human verification before publishing.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restart in Safe Mode to Rule Out an App Overlay
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm whether an app is affecting rendering
steps: Boot the device into Safe Mode.
Check whether the display looks normal with only pre-installed apps active.
If normal, uninstall the most recently added app suspected of causing the issue.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Same caveat as disp-010/disp-011 - source not fully verified.

merged_variants: pictures look fuzzy even in good light
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Clean All Camera Lenses
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove smudges causing soft focus
steps: Use a soft, dry, microfiber cloth to wipe all lenses on the device.
Clean the main, ultra-wide, telephoto, and any auxiliary preview/rangefinding lenses.

merged_variants: pictures look fuzzy even in good light
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Turn On Focus Enhancer for Close-Range Shots
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reduce blur around close subjects
steps: Open the Camera app.
Tap the flower icon on the preview screen to turn on Focus enhancer.
This automatically switches to the ultra-wide camera at close range to reduce blur.

merged_variants: pictures look fuzzy even in good light
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Remove a Camera Lens Protector or Cover
troubleshooting_records.description: It will eliminate protector-induced focus distortion
steps: Remove any third-party camera lens protector or cover.
Take a test photo without it to see if focus and clarity improve.

merged_variants: camera blurry at close range with high zoom
telephoto zoom out of focus up close
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Respect Minimum Shooting Distance on High Zoom (Ultra models)
troubleshooting_records.description: It will avoid the telephoto camera's close-range blur
steps: At high zoom, the device automatically switches to the telephoto camera, which is designed for distant subjects.
Keep at least the minimum shooting distance for the model: 30 cm on the Galaxy S25 Ultra, 80 cm on the Galaxy S26 Ultra.
Move back to the correct distance before shooting for a clearer result.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S26 Ultra (telephoto minimum distances)

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Understand Normal Optical Blur in 200MP Mode (Ultra models)
troubleshooting_records.description: It will explain expected partial-frame softness
steps: Recognize that the camera's focus range varies with aperture, shooting distance, and subject position in the 200MP high-resolution setting.
Some parts of the frame appearing soft in this mode is a normal optical characteristic, not necessarily a defect.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Allow Internal Condensation to Clear Naturally
troubleshooting_records.description: It will let temporary fogging dissipate on its own
steps: Recognize haze can be caused by internal condensation from a temperature difference inside/outside the device.
Wait for the condensation to clear naturally; the device can be used normally in the meantime.
Do not attempt to dry the lens by force (e.g., heat) as this is unnecessary and can cause damage.

merged_variants: dark lines appear while recording video
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Treat Dark Lines During Capture as a Flicker-Related Issue
troubleshooting_records.description: It will connect capture banding to lighting/refresh causes
steps: If dark lines or flicker appear specifically while taking photos or videos, treat this as related to lighting flicker or refresh-rate interaction rather than a separate defect.
Follow the screen_flickering_camera_specific record (disp-006) guidance to add more light to the scene.
troubleshooting_records.notes: The source article references this scenario but the full explanatory steps were truncated in retrieval.

merged_variants: camera makes noise when moving phone
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Recognize Signs of OIS Hardware Damage
troubleshooting_records.description: It will identify a hardware fault versus a software one
steps: Optical image stabilization uses gyroscope readings to counter camera shake; repeated strong vibration or drops can damage this mechanism.
Signs include images appearing constantly shaken, or audible/visible movement of the camera module.
This is a hardware issue; software troubleshooting will not resolve it -- schedule a repair.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Sourced from iFixit (third-party repair reference), not an official Samsung support article; treat as directional guidance pending official confirmation.

merged_variants: pictures look fuzzy even in good light
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check Camera Assistant Shutter/ISO Settings (Good Lock)
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove slow-shutter blur from Camera Assistant limits
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Camera app > Quick controls > Settings > Camera Assistant
steps: Note: Camera Assistant is only available in countries supporting the Good Lock app.
Open the Camera app, tap Quick controls, then Settings, then Camera Assistant.
Tap Advanced Photo mode controls, then set Minimum shutter speed and Maximum ISO to None.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy devices in regions/models supporting Good Lock's Camera Assistant

merged_variants: pictures look fuzzy even in good light
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Follow General Blur/Dark Photo Guidance and Confirm Software Is Current
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out a stale camera-app software build
steps: Confirm the device software and Camera app are on the latest available version.
Retest photo/video quality after updating.
If issues persist, Samsung support will check device condition and confirm no app is interfering with the camera.
troubleshooting_records.notes: S015 page content was mostly navigation chrome in the fetch; core steps summarized from the page's stated intent, not a full step-by-step capture.

troubleshooting_records.description: It will let you choose navigation type
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Tap Navigation bar.
Select Buttons or Swipe gestures as your preferred navigation type.

merged_variants: swipe navigation feels wrong after installing app
gesture navigation moves up/down instead of left/right
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Adjust Swipe Gesture Order and Sensitivity
troubleshooting_records.description: It will fine-tune how swipe gestures respond
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Display > Navigation bar > Swipe gestures > More options
steps: Open Settings > Display > Navigation bar.
Select Swipe gestures, then tap More options.
Select the desired swipe gesture and button order, and adjust Gesture sensitivity.

merged_variants: swipe navigation feels wrong after installing app
gesture navigation moves up/down instead of left/right
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Enable Block Gestures With S Pen (S Pen devices)
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop accidental edge swipes while drawing
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Display > Navigation bar > Swipe gestures
steps: Open Settings > Display > Navigation bar > Swipe gestures.
Turn on Block Gestures with S Pen to prevent accidental navigation while drawing near screen edges.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy devices with S Pen support

merged_variants: swipe from bottom gesture missing after update
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restore Removed Legacy Gestures via Good Lock NavStar
troubleshooting_records.description: It will bring back Swipe from bottom and Gesture hints
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Good Lock app > Make up > NavStar
steps: Note: Recent navigation bar updates removed the 'Swipe from bottom' option and 'Gesture hints' from the standard menu.
Download Good Lock from the Galaxy Store and open it.
Select the Make up tab, find NavStar, and tap the download icon.
Open NavStar, tap Start, then Allow, then turn on the Swipe gestures switch.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy devices supporting the Good Lock app
troubleshooting_records.notes: This addresses a One UI navigation-bar redesign that removed legacy options from the base Settings menu; confirm current Good Lock/NavStar availability for the user's region before advising.

merged_variants: swipe navigation feels wrong after installing app
gesture navigation moves up/down instead of left/right
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Use the Corner-Swipe Shortcut for the Digital Assistant Regardless of Navigation Type
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clarify an always-available gesture
steps: Regardless of whether Buttons or Swipe gestures is selected, swiping inward from a bottom corner of the screen opens the digital assistant.
This is expected behavior, not a misconfiguration, if the user reports an unexpected assistant launch during swipes.

merged_variants: swipe navigation feels wrong after installing app
gesture navigation moves up/down instead of left/right
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Activate Circle to Search via Home Button/Handle
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clarify a touch-and-hold gesture distinct from navigation
steps: Touch and hold the Home button or the navigation handle at the bottom of the screen to activate Circle to Search.
This is separate from the left/right or up/down swipe navigation gestures.

merged_variants: swipe navigation feels wrong after installing app
gesture navigation moves up/down instead of left/right
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for a Conflicting Third-Party Launcher or Gesture App
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm whether a downloaded app changed gesture behavior
steps: Boot the device into Safe Mode, which disables third-party apps.
Test the swipe navigation direction in Safe Mode.
If gestures behave normally in Safe Mode, uninstall the most recently installed launcher, gesture, or accessibility app.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Safe Mode isolation is a general Samsung troubleshooting pattern (seen across battery/display/app articles); no official article specifically ties Safe Mode to gesture-direction complaints, so this record is an inferred application of a verified general technique -- flagged for review.

merged_variants: phone got slow after the update

apps started lagging after the update
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Allow the Device to Settle After an Update
troubleshooting_records.description: It will let background optimization finish
steps: Turn the phone off completely.
Turn it back on to perform a soft reboot.
Wait a few minutes for the system to settle and optimize apps after the update.

merged_variants: phone got slow after the update
phone became laggy after software update
apps started lagging after the update
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Wipe the Cache Partition via Recovery Mode
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear stale system cache after an update
steps: Turn off the device.
Press and hold Volume Up + Power key until the Android Recovery screen appears, then release.
Use Volume Down to highlight Wipe cache partition, press Power to select it, then confirm Yes.
Select Reboot system now.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Wiping cache does not delete personal data, per the source.

merged_variants: phone got slow after the update
phone became laggy after software update
apps started lagging after the update
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Perform a Factory Reset if Lag Persists After Update
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove leftover or conflicting system files
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Factory data reset
steps: Back up all important data first.
Go to Settings and perform a factory reset.
Confirm the reset to remove leftover or conflicting system files from the update.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Source notes post-update lag or glitches are often temporary and resolve after system optimization -- reset should be a later step, not a first response.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for Software Updates
troubleshooting_records.description: It will apply bug fixes and compatibility improvements
steps: Open Settings and tap Software update.
Tap Download and install, then Install now if an update is available.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Close All Recently Used Apps
troubleshooting_records.description: It will free active memory tied up by open apps
steps: Tap the Recents button (left of the Home button, or accessed via the navigation gesture).
Tap Close all.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Clean Memory via Device Care
troubleshooting_records.description: It will free RAM by stopping background apps
steps: Open Settings and tap Device care.
Tap Memory, then tap Clean now.
Optionally tap Excluded apps to keep specific apps running in the background.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restart the Device
troubleshooting_records.description: It will refresh the system and close stuck processes
steps: Swipe down from the top right of the screen to open the Quick panel.
Tap the Power off icon, then tap Restart.
Alternatively, hold the Side key and Volume down key together for more than 7 seconds.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Run Self-Diagnostics in Samsung Members
troubleshooting_records.description: It will identify what is causing the slowdown
steps: Open the Samsung Members app.
Tap Phone diagnostics in the Support tab.
Tap the icon for the feature to test, or tap Test all.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check and Free Up Storage Space
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove the low-storage cause of slowdown
steps: Open Settings and tap Device care (or Battery and device care).
Tap Storage to review usage.
Delete large or unneeded files, or clear the Trash, if storage is nearly full.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Enable Auto Restart on a Schedule
troubleshooting_records.description: It will keep performance consistent over time
steps: Open Settings and tap Device care.
Find Auto restart and turn it on.
Optionally set a schedule for when the device should restart automatically.

merged_variants: one ui update made phone slower
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Do a Clean App Reinstall Instead of a Restore After a Major One UI Update
troubleshooting_records.description: It will avoid carrying over incompatible app data
steps: After a major One UI or Android version update, consider setting up the device fresh rather than restoring via Smart Switch.
Reinstall only the apps you actively use from the Play Store or Galaxy Store.
This avoids carrying over app data from versions not yet optimized for the new OS, which is a common cause of post-update slowdowns and battery drain.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Sourced from a Samsung Community user discussion, not an official Samsung support article. Presented as a commonly reported community workaround, not verified Samsung guidance -- recommend human review before treating as authoritative.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check Current Storage Usage
troubleshooting_records.description: It will show a breakdown of what is using space
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Battery and device care > Storage
steps: Open Settings and tap Battery and device care.
Tap Storage to see total space used and a breakdown by file type.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Run Optimize Now / Clean Now From Device Care
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear temporary and junk files quickly
steps: Open Settings and tap Device care.
Tap Optimize now for an all-in-one cleanup pass.
Or tap Storage, then Clean now for a storage-focused pass.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Empty the Recycle Bin / Trash
troubleshooting_records.description: It will permanently remove already-deleted files
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Device care > Storage > Recycle bin
steps: Open Settings > Device care > Storage.
Under Recycle bin, tap the app icon holding trashed files (e.g., Gallery).
Tap Empty, then confirm to permanently delete.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Marked critical because emptying Trash is an irreversible deletion, unlike moving files to Trash.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Uninstall Unused Apps
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove apps that have not been used recently
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Device care > Storage > Unused apps
steps: Open Settings > Device care > Storage.
Tap Unused apps.
Select the apps to remove and tap Uninstall.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Remove Duplicate Files
troubleshooting_records.description: It will find and delete exact-copy files
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Device care > Storage > Duplicate files
steps: Open Settings > Device care > Storage.
Tap Duplicate files.
Review the list and delete confirmed duplicates.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Delete Files by Category Using My Files or Device Care
troubleshooting_records.description: It will let you selectively clear large file types
steps: Open Settings > Device care > Storage, or open the My Files app.
Tap a file category such as Images, Videos, Audio files, or Documents.
Select unneeded files and tap Delete or Delete all, then confirm Move to Trash.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Clear App Cache for Specific Apps
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reclaim space used by temporary app data
steps: Open Settings and tap Apps.
Select or search for the app.
Tap Storage, then tap Clear cache.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Distinct from Clear data, which removes logins and saved app data as well.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Move Files to an SD Card (Supported Models)
troubleshooting_records.description: It will offload storage without deleting files
steps: Open the My Files app.
Select the files or folders to move.
Tap Move, then choose the SD card as the destination.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy devices with a microSD card slot

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Clean Memory (RAM) to Complement Storage Cleanup
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop background apps from slowing the device
steps: Open Settings and tap Device care.
Tap Memory, then tap Clean now.
Add frequently needed apps to Excluded apps if you don't want them stopped.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for App and Software Updates
troubleshooting_records.description: It will apply bug fixes for the crashing app
steps: Open Settings and tap Software update; install any available update.
Open the Play Store or Galaxy Store, go to Manage apps & device, and update the specific app.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Stabilize the Network Connection
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out connectivity as the crash cause
steps: Turn off mobile data or the Wi-Fi router for a few minutes.
Turn the device off and restart it.
Turn mobile data or Wi-Fi back on and reconnect, then retest the app.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Clear the App's Cache and Data
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove corrupted app data causing crashes
steps: Open Settings and tap Apps.
Select the crashing app.
Tap Storage, then Clear cache; if crashing continues, tap Clear data (this signs you out and erases local app data).

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Free Up Device Storage
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove the low-storage cause of app failures
steps: Open Settings > Device care > Storage.
Delete unneeded large files or unused apps to free space.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Boot Into Safe Mode to Isolate a Third-Party App Conflict
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm if another app is interfering
steps: Boot the device into Safe Mode.
Test whether the crashing app behaves normally.
If it does, a different downloaded app is likely conflicting; uninstall recently added apps one at a time.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Disable Battery Optimization for the Affected App
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop background restrictions from killing the app
steps: Open the app's settings within Settings > Apps > [app].
Find battery-related options and disable optimization/restriction for that app.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Uninstall and Reinstall the App
troubleshooting_records.description: It will replace a corrupted install with a clean one
steps: Uninstall the app from the device.
Restart the device.
Reinstall the app from the Google Play Store or Galaxy Store.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check if the App-Specific Crash Is a Known Developer-Side Issue
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm whether the fix depends on the app developer
steps: Check the app's reviews in the Play Store/Galaxy Store for similar recent complaints.
If it's a known widespread bug (e.g., a specific version of a third-party app), keep the app updated and wait for the developer's fix, since Samsung cannot alter third-party app code.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Reset App Preferences as a Broader Fix
troubleshooting_records.description: It will restore default settings for all apps at once
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Reset app preferences
steps: Open Settings and tap General management (or Apps, depending on One UI version).
Tap Reset, then Reset app preferences.
Confirm; this re-enables disabled apps and resets default app choices without deleting data.
troubleshooting_records.notes: This step is a standard Android/One UI reset option referenced generally across app-troubleshooting guidance; exact menu location varies by One UI version.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Perform a Factory Reset if the Device Crashes Regardless of App
troubleshooting_records.description: It will resolve a device-wide instability issue
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Factory data reset
steps: If crashing/freezing happens across many different apps (not just one), back up your data.
Open Settings, search for and select Factory data reset, and complete the reset.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Toggle Wi-Fi Off and On
troubleshooting_records.description: It will refresh a stuck wireless connection
steps: Open the Quick panel and turn Wi-Fi off.
Wait a few seconds, then turn Wi-Fi back on and reconnect.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Forget and Re-Add the Wi-Fi Network
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rebuild a corrupted saved network profile
steps: Open Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi.
Tap the gear icon next to the network, then tap Forget.
Reconnect to the network and re-enter the password.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Reset Network Settings
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear all saved Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/mobile configs
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Reset Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings
steps: Open Settings and tap General management.
Tap Reset, then Reset Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings.
Tap Reset settings to confirm.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check and Update the Router Firmware
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out router-side instability
steps: Confirm the router firmware is updated to the latest version.
Check whether the Wi-Fi network appears normally on other devices.
If the network is undetected on other devices too, contact the router manufacturer for support.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Power-Cycle the Router
troubleshooting_records.description: It will resolve a router-side stall or glitch
steps: Disconnect and reconnect the router's power cable.
Wait for it to fully restart, then retry connecting.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Run Samsung Members Wi-Fi Diagnostics
troubleshooting_records.description: It will check for a device-side wireless fault
steps: Open the Samsung Members app and tap Support.
Tap Get started to run the diagnostics scan.
Select Wi-Fi and follow the on-screen instructions, then review the results.

merged_variants: wifi switches to mobile data automatically
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Disable Intelligent Wi-Fi / Auto Network Switching
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop the phone from auto-leaving a 'weak' network
steps: Open Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi.
Tap the three-dot menu, then Intelligent Wi-Fi.
Turn off options like Switch to mobile data or Auto network switching.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Sourced from Samsung Community user reports (not an official Samsung support article) describing the Intelligent Wi-Fi menu; exact toggle names may differ by One UI version and carrier.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Assign a Static IP or Re-Add With a Fixed Address
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out DHCP lease conflicts
steps: Open Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi, tap the saved network's gear icon.
Tap View more (or IP settings), and switch from DHCP to Static.
Enter an appropriate static IP address outside the router's DHCP range.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Referenced via a linked support article (TSG01001559) in a community thread; not independently fetched, so treat menu wording as approximate.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check if Mute All Sounds (Accessibility) Is Enabled
troubleshooting_records.description: It will restore all audio output if muted system-wide
steps: Open Settings and tap Accessibility.
Tap Hearing enhancements.
Check whether Mute all sounds is enabled, and turn it off if so.
troubleshooting_records.notes: When Mute all sounds is enabled, volume cannot be adjusted at all, including during calls.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Turn Off Do Not Disturb
troubleshooting_records.description: It will remove a notification-silencing mode
steps: Open Settings > Notifications > Do not disturb.
Make sure it is turned off.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check Left/Right Sound Balance
troubleshooting_records.description: It will fix audio that seems to favor one side
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Accessibility > Hearing enhancements > Left/right sound balance
steps: Open Settings > Accessibility > Hearing enhancements.
Tap Left/right sound balance and ensure the slider is centered.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Disable Separate App Sound if Not Needed
troubleshooting_records.description: It will stop audio being routed to an unintended output
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > Sounds and vibration > Separate app sound
steps: Open Settings > Sounds and vibration > Separate app sound.
Turn it off unless you intentionally route a specific app's audio elsewhere.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Remove Connected Audio Accessories and Disable Bluetooth
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm audio isn't being routed externally
steps: Remove any connected accessories such as earphones or external devices.
Turn off Bluetooth from the Quick panel.
Check that speaker openings are not blocked by a case or dirt.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restart the Device
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear a temporary audio-routing glitch
steps: Press and hold the Power + Volume down buttons.
Or use the Quick panel Power icon and tap Restart.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Test Audio in Safe Mode
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm whether a downloaded app is muting audio
steps: Press and hold Power + Volume down, then long-press Power off and tap Safe mode.
Play audio on the device; if sound works, a downloaded app is likely the cause.
Delete recently installed apps one by one, restarting and testing after each removal.
Turn the device off and back on to exit Safe mode.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Dry the Device if It Has Gotten Wet
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear water blocking the speaker or earpiece
steps: If the device has gotten wet, dry it immediately with a clean, soft cloth.
Pay careful attention to the earpiece, microphones, speaker, and USB port.
Avoid exposing the device to salt water or ionized water.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for a Blocked Air Vent Under a Case
troubleshooting_records.description: It will fix muffled sound caused by a covered vent
steps: Check whether a phone case or protective film is covering the air vent hole near the camera lens (used for water resistance).
Remove or adjust the case if it is blocking this vent.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Reset All Settings if the Issue Persists
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear a stubborn system-level audio fault
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Reset all settings
steps: Open Settings > General management > Reset > Reset all settings.
Enter your password if required and complete the reset.
Play audio to confirm whether the issue is fixed.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Escalate to Samsung Service if Sound Issues Persist
troubleshooting_records.description: It will get the speaker hardware inspected
steps: If the speaker or sound issue still persists after completing all software steps,
visit a Samsung Service Centre or book a repair for further assistance.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Recognize Normal Heat-Generating Scenarios
troubleshooting_records.description: It will explain expected warmth versus a problem
steps: Understand it is normal for the device to warm up during high-power tasks like fast charging, gaming, or streaming.
Also expect warmth during initial setup or large data restores.
Only treat the device as having an issue if it feels excessively or uncomfortably hot.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Stop Use and Let the Device Cool Immediately
troubleshooting_records.description: It will prevent thermal shutdown and protect hardware
steps: If the device feels uncomfortably warm, close all running apps.
Disconnect any charger.
Stop using the device until it cools down completely.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Inspect Charging Hardware for Overheating Causes
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out a damaged cable or blocked wireless pad
steps: Unplug the charger and allow the device to cool before resuming.
Check the cable and port for fraying or damage; replace with a genuine Samsung accessory if needed.
Ensure no foreign objects (metal, magnets, cards) sit between the device and a wireless charging pad.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Update Software for Thermal Management Improvements
troubleshooting_records.description: It will apply the latest thermal-management firmware
steps: Open Settings and tap Software update.
Install any available update, since Samsung ships thermal-management improvements through software updates.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Turn Off Unused Connectivity Features
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reduce background heat from radios
steps: Open the Quick Settings panel.
Toggle off Wi-Fi, Location (GPS), and Bluetooth when not actively in use.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Lower the Screen Refresh Rate
troubleshooting_records.description: It will reduce power draw contributing to heat
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Tap Motion smoothness.
Select Standard to lower the refresh rate and conserve power.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Galaxy devices with a variable/high refresh-rate display (e.g., Galaxy S24, Galaxy Z Fold)

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restart the Device to Clear Conflicting Background Apps
troubleshooting_records.description: It will resolve software conflicts generating heat
steps: Restart the device to clear temporary software conflicts between running apps.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Understand Automatic Thermal Protection Behavior
troubleshooting_records.description: It will explain automatic slow-downs and shutdowns
steps: Know that if the device overheats, Samsung's safeguard may limit screen brightness and performance speed and stop battery charging.
Running apps may be closed and calling features limited except for emergency calls, until it cools.
If a second, more severe warning appears, the device may power off automatically to prevent damage.

merged_variants: phone hot and battery draining fast
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check Battery Health When Overheating Recurs Without Heavy Use
troubleshooting_records.description: It will identify a failing battery as the heat source
steps: If the device overheats even during light use, note that a battery nearing end-of-life can generate more heat than normal.
Run the Samsung Members battery diagnostic to check condition.
If diagnostics indicate poor battery health, schedule a battery replacement.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Sourced from iFixit (third-party repair reference), not an official Samsung support article.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Review Common Touch-Sensitivity Interference Factors
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out accessory or condition interference
steps: Check whether a third-party screen protector or case is affecting touch response, especially if dust/air is trapped under it or it is peeling at the edges.
Note that wearing gloves, having wet or unclean hands, or using sharp objects can also prevent proper touch detection.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restart the Device
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear a temporary system error affecting touch
steps: Press and hold the Side key and Volume down key together for more than 7 seconds until the device restarts automatically.
If the touchscreen is completely unresponsive, this button-combination restart does not require touch input.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Increase Touch Sensitivity for Screen Protector Use
troubleshooting_records.description: It will compensate for a protector dulling touch response
steps: Open Settings and tap Display.
Turn on Touch sensitivity to improve response through a screen protector or tempered glass.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Remove a Non-Genuine Screen Protector or Case
troubleshooting_records.description: It will eliminate an accessory causing dead zones
steps: Remove any non-genuine screen protector or case, particularly near the screen edges.
Retest touch response without the accessory attached.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check if TalkBack Is Accidentally Enabled
troubleshooting_records.description: It will restore normal single-tap behavior
steps: If voice guidance plays when touching the screen and gestures behave differently (single tap to select, double-tap to open), TalkBack may be enabled.
Open Settings > Accessibility > TalkBack and turn it off if it was not intentionally enabled.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Run Samsung Members Touchscreen Diagnostics
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm whether the touch digitizer is faulty
steps: Open the Samsung Members app and tap Support.
Tap Get started to begin the diagnostics scan.
Select Touch screen and follow the on-screen instructions, then review results.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check for Moisture on the Screen
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out water interference with touch detection
steps: Wipe the touchscreen to ensure it is free from moisture, since humid conditions or water exposure can cause malfunction.
Retest touch response once fully dry.

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Check Charger for Damage if Touch Fails While Charging
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out charger interference with the touch panel
steps: If the touchscreen malfunctions specifically while charging, a damaged charger may not supply clean power to the device.
Test with a different genuine Samsung charger to see if touch response improves.

merged_variants: touchscreen stopped working after software update
touch doesn't respond after update but S Pen still works
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Wipe Cache Partition if Touch Failure Started Right After an Update
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear a corrupted post-update cache
steps: Turn off the device.
Press and hold Volume Up and the Side/Power button until the Samsung logo appears and a vibration is felt, then release.
In recovery mode, highlight Wipe cache partition, select it, and confirm.
Reboot the system and retest touch response.
troubleshooting_records.device_scope: Devices with a physical S Pen (workaround verified using S Pen input to navigate)
troubleshooting_records.notes: This specific update-triggered scenario and wipe-cache workaround were reported in a Samsung Community thread rather than confirmed in an official Samsung troubleshooting article; recommend human review, and note the community poster indicated the wipe did not fully resolve their case (hardware replacement was ultimately needed).

merged_variants: touch not working in some areas
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Escalate to Service if Touch Issues Persist
troubleshooting_records.description: It will get the digitizer hardware inspected
steps: If touch issues continue after all software troubleshooting, this may indicate a hardware fault.
Visit a Samsung walk-in service center or schedule a repair service online.

merged_variants: phone charging much slower than before
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Charge at Room Temperature
troubleshooting_records.description: It will avoid the safeguard that slows charging in heat/cold
steps: Avoid charging in direct sunlight, a hot car, or very cold environments.
If the device or environment is too hot or too cold, a safeguard automatically slows charging speed to protect the battery.

merged_variants: phone won't turn on after connecting charger
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Wait for a Minimum Charge Before Powering On a Fully Depleted Device
troubleshooting_records.description: It will explain why the phone doesn't turn on immediately
steps: If the battery was completely depleted, the device will not power on immediately even with the charger connected.
Let it charge for a few minutes until it reaches at least 1%, then try powering it on.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Restart the Device to Refresh the Mobile Data Connection
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clear a stuck network session
steps: Open the Power menu (hold Power, or use the Quick settings Power icon).
Tap Restart, then tap Restart again to confirm.
The device will shut down and automatically reboot.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Free Up Storage if It Is Affecting Data Performance
troubleshooting_records.description: It will rule out low storage as a contributing cause
steps: Open Device care and check available storage.
Clean up storage if space is low, since insufficient storage can affect overall device and network responsiveness.
Back up extra files using Smart Switch or a Samsung/Google account before deleting.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Boot Into Safe Mode to Rule Out an App Interfering With Data
troubleshooting_records.description: It will confirm whether a downloaded app is the cause
steps: Certain downloaded apps can affect network connectivity in addition to causing freezes or crashes.
Boot into Safe Mode, which disables downloaded apps, and test mobile data speed.
If speed improves in Safe Mode, uninstall the suspect app.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Distinguish Expected Post-Update Sluggishness From an Update Failure
troubleshooting_records.description: It will clarify whether the slowdown is temporary or a failed update
steps: Recognize the device may feel slightly sluggish after a firmware update due to enhancements or new background features settling in.
Separately, consider whether the update was interrupted (e.g., lost internet connection mid-update), which can cause lasting performance problems rather than temporary ones.
Also consider that a large number of installed apps with background processes (messengers, games, anti-virus apps) independently slows the device and can be mistaken for an update-caused issue.

merged_variants: phone got slow after the update
phone became laggy after software update
apps started lagging after the update
troubleshooting_records.action_name: Factory Reset if Firmware Corruption Is Suspected
troubleshooting_records.description: It will resolve performance issues tied to firmware corruption
troubleshooting_records.settings_path: Settings > General management > Reset > Factory data reset
steps: Follow the prompts until the device reboots to begin a Factory Data Reset.
After the device fully loads, check whether performance has improved.
If the issue persists, this may indicate firmware corruption or a device-level fault requiring service.

troubleshooting_records.action_name: Clear the Cache for Always On Display if Flicker Follows Wireless Charging or AOD Use
troubleshooting_records.description: It will address a community-reported AOD-cache flicker pattern
steps: If flickering appears mainly after using Always On Display or placing the device on a wireless charger, try clearing the cache for the Always On Display / clock app.
Open Settings > Apps, find the relevant clock/AOD component, tap Storage, then Clear cache.
Retest by using the wireless charger and observing AOD behavior afterward.
troubleshooting_records.notes: Sourced from a Samsung Community user thread describing a personal workaround (clearing AOD cache), not confirmed as official Samsung guidance. The same user reported the flicker recurred intermittently afterward, so this should be treated as partial/unverified relief rather than a confirmed fix.
